ns2:section.sectionText: Political Violence This course surveys various forms of political violence and examines competing theories about why these types of violence occur and their implications. It is organized to analyze different "categories" of violence, all of which constitute pressing topics in international relations and comparative politics. These categories include protests, revolt, and revolution; riots; repression; coups; rebel movements; civil war and ethnic conflict; genocide and massacres; anti-occupation insurgency, secessionism and partition; terrorism; and a session exploring paths to political non-violence or reconciliation. Theoretical readings will often be supplemented by case studies. The course is a discussion-based seminar that meets twice weekly.
ns2:section.sectionNotes: Restricted to students with Sophomore, Junior, or Senior class standing.
